# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 61 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 61 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_061_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

This chapter bridges Similitude 5 and Similitude 6 with a vision of the Angel of Righteousness adjudicating repentance. The two categories emerging are: (1) those given repentance — they leave joyfully; (2) those denied repentance — they leave sorrowfully. A third, ambiguous category of "doubters" receives repentance "in proportion to the disposition of their heart."

The question about those who died before "these days of repentance" (*pro tōn hēmerōn toutōn*) reflects the Hermatine awareness that his message of a second repentance opportunity was historically bounded. Those who died before this window was opened — is there hope? Hermas's answer is oblique.

The closing warning against the devil in 61:5 echoes the Mandates (ch. 47). The devil's strategy with double-minded people is consistent throughout the work.

---

## Similitude 5, Part 7 — The Angel of Righteousness and Repentance

**61:1** "I should like to know, lord," I said, "whether those who died before these days of repentance have any hope." "Come," he said, "and I will show you concerning all those who have doubted and sinned."

**61:2** He showed me a young man sitting in a chair, addressing many people. "Do you see this young man?" he asked. "I see him, lord," I replied. "He is the angel of righteousness," he said. "Standing around him are many people of various kinds. Some are being brought before him; some are going away with joy; and some are going away with grief."

**61:3** "And many are standing around listening. Some who come forward go away joyful; others grieve and weep." "Lord," I said, "I do not understand what all this means." "Listen," he said. "The young man sitting on the chair is the angel of righteousness. Those brought before him are those who are to receive repentance. Hear also why some go away joyful and some sorrowful."

**61:4** "Those who go away joyful are those who have received these words into their hearts and repented with their whole heart. To them repentance has been given. But those who go away sorrowful are those who have turned completely away from God and do not repent. To these, repentance of life is not given."

**61:5** "But what of those who doubted?" "And what of those who sinned but have not repented?" I asked. "To those who doubted," he said, "repentance is given in proportion to the disposition of their heart." And he said to me: "Do not give the devil a foothold in your heart. He is crafty and devious in turning aside the servants of God — especially those who are double-minded. So be firm in your faith and do not waver."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
